content: Ciprofloxacin is a synthetic broad-spectrum antimicrobial agent designed for oral administration. It is available in two forms: CIPRO tablets and CIPRO oral suspension. The active ingredient, ciprofloxacin hydrochloride, is a fluoroquinolone and chemically described as the monohydrochloride monohydrate salt of 1-cyclopropyl-6-fluoro-1,4-dihydro-4-oxo-7-(1-piperazinyl)-3-quinolinecarboxylic acid. Its empirical formula is C17H18FN3O3·HCl·H2O. Ciprofloxacin appears as a faintly yellowish to light yellow crystalline substance. The chemical structure of ciprofloxacin is consistent with its description as 1-cyclopropyl-6-fluoro-1,4-dihydro-4-oxo-7-(1-piperazinyl)-3-quinolinecarboxylic acid. CIPRO film-coated tablets are available in strengths of 250 mg and 500 mg (ciprofloxacin equivalent). These tablets are white to slightly yellowish in color. The inactive ingredients in the tablets include corn starch, microcrystalline cellulose, silicon dioxide, crospovidone, magnesium stearate, hypromellose, titanium dioxide, and polyethylene glycol. Ciprofloxacin oral suspension is available in two concentrations: 5% (5 g ciprofloxacin per 100 mL) and 10% (10 g ciprofloxacin per 100 mL). The suspension is white to slightly yellowish in appearance, with a strawberry flavor, and may contain yellow-orange droplets. It is composed of ciprofloxacin microcapsules and a diluent, which are mixed prior to dispensing. The microcapsules contain ciprofloxacin, povidone, methacrylic acid copolymer, hypromellose, magnesium stearate, and polysorbate 20. The diluent includes medium-chain triglycerides, sucrose, lecithin, water, and strawberry flavor. Each 5% suspension contains 3 g of sucrose per 100 mL. Inactive components of the suspension include mineral oil and white petrolatum. The pH of the suspension is adjusted using hydrochloric acid and/or sodium hydroxide. The osmolality of the suspension is approximately 300 mOsm. Ciprofloxacin is also available as a 2% ready-to-use infusion solution in 5% dextrose injection. This formulation contains lactic acid as a solubilizing agent and hydrochloric acid for pH adjustment. The infusion solution is packaged in a latex-free plastic container made from specially formulated polyvinyl chloride. The suitability of the plastic container has been confirmed through animal testing and tissue culture toxicity studies, as per USP biological tests for plastic containers. The glucose content in the infusion solution is 5 g for the 100 mL bag and 10 g for the 200 mL flexible container.
